clue.text: Picture king amongst group of pieces leading to check

indicators.note: something amongst a group sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a set is a group of matching pieces, as in a chess set
K is the chess abbreviation for king
CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: the king moves among a group of pieces before delivering check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture hides abbreviations: the king sits inside the set, and check follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing is a picture, so the noun works as a synonym here.

clue.text: Sign of injury, with nobody removing ring when entering hospital device

indicators.note: whatever is entering goes inside something else, so it is placed within another word

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so one letter is taken out of a word

parts.note: none means no one
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: An injury mark seen on a hospital scan, with nobody left wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring is the round letter O, a standard crossword convention; 'hospital device' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scanner is imaging equipment used in hospitals, such as an MRI or CT machine.

clue.text: Congress heading off cheers about Republican addition?

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word is wrapped round another
with its heading off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse
ta is British informal thanks
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Political news: Congress, minus its leader, cheering over a Republican amendment.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress is not the US legislature but sexual congress; drop its first letter, then wrap TA around R.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something added beyond the usual, so it is a synonym for an addition.

clue.text: College, stretched, failed

parts.note: C is a common abbreviation for college
the rack was a torture device that stretched its victims

explanation.surface: A student at college, under strain, flunked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has cracked has broken down or given way, so it has failed.

clue.text: Attractive woman's detailed incantation

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, meaning the tail end of the word is cut off

parts.note: a mantrap is slang for a seductive woman

explanation.surface: A seductive woman recites a spell in elaborate detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as elaborate, but it means de-tailed: the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly in meditation, a kind of incantation.

clue.text: One suffers effects of sunburn, having rolled over in a doze

indicators.note: rolling over turns something end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sunburnt skin peels
a means one

explanation.surface: A sunbather, burnt and peeling, turns over while dozing on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One suffers' as A plus PEELS, then turn the whole lot round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is in a doze, so the adjective matches the phrase.

clue.text: Tense before translation of Wooster comedy finally displaying more elevated level?

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: a translation turns one form into another, so the letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: the letters of the name rearranged

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A translated Wodehouse comedy about Bertie Wooster shows him reaching a higher level.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is P G Wodehouse's comic hero, which makes 'comedy' look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-storey building has an upper floor, so it reaches a higher level; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Bovine material in test mostly upheld as source of ventilation

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means read from the bottom upwards
in places one piece inside another
mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a test
cud is what cows chew

explanation.surface: A lab sample of cow matter is put on test, held up, as a way to air the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Bovine material is cud, the food cows chew a second time; in a down clue 'upheld' means the letters read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An air duct is a pipe carrying air through a building, so it supplies ventilation.

clue.text: Remarkable gains least expected after damage in these constituencies

definitions.text: Remarkable gains least expected after damage in these constituencies

indicators.note: read as re-mark-able, something that can be marked out again in a new arrangement

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Election night: in these constituencies, surprising gains are likely after a damaging campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while the anagram after MAR builds it; 'Remarkable' suggests re-marking the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal seats are constituencies held by narrow majorities, where a party can easily gain or lose.

clue.text: Strained sound of rebuke muffling answer

indicators.note: muffling wraps something up to deaden it, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: tut is the click of disapproval
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A tense tutting stifles someone's reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight is taut, which is the same as strained or stretched.

clue.text: American trips taking in crumbling hall on an irregular basis

indicators.note: something crumbling falls apart, so its letters break up and resettle

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: tours are trips
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: American tourists visit a crumbling old hall whenever they feel like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at all hours means at any time, without a regular schedule.

clue.text: Reveal hesitation about nationalist question

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation
N abbreviates nationalist
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A politician hesitates over a question about nationalism, then reveals all.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask someone is to expose their true identity, so it is a synonym of reveal.

clue.text: Extinct bird mentioned in dreary lecture

indicators.note: a thing mentioned is spoken, so it is the sound of the words that counts

parts.note: grey means dreary and a talk is a lecture

explanation.surface: An extinct bird gets a passing mention in a tedious lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, a grey talk runs together into the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The great auk was a large flightless seabird, hunted to extinction in the 1840s.

clue.text: Power gap filled by party leader

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: a gap filled by something has that thing put inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or gap
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A power vacuum is filled by the leader of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like the definition, but party belongs to the wordplay and leader stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation, so a leader.

clue.text: Electrical equipment linking birch and shrub

parts.note: a birch and a switch are both thin rods for beating
box is an evergreen shrub used for hedges

explanation.surface: An electrical device connecting a birch tree to a shrub, as if wiring the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchbox is a housing holding electrical switches, a piece of electrical equipment.

clue.text: Rumour I ignored — it's not sweet

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: bruit is an old word for a rumour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a rumour, insisting it is anything but sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the term for very dry champagne or sparkling wine, the opposite of sweet.

clue.text: Large organ broke? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of it, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: A large church organ, broken? Not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Large organ suggests a church instrument, but it is the body's largest organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin is the largest organ of the human body by area.

clue.text: Small support for hosting a composer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a truss is a supporting frame or brace
taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest support system hosting a visiting composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a composer' reads as one phrase, but the a belongs to the wordplay and composer alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann and Richard Strauss were famous composers, so the surname names one.

clue.text: Ministers not entirely caring about first one leaving wild party

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
not entirely means falling short of the whole, so the last letter goes

parts.note: clement means merciful or kind

indicators.note: the first one leaving means the opening letter departs from the word

parts.note: an orgy is a wild party

explanation.surface: Government ministers, less than caring, leave a wild party first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first one leaving' removes the first letter of the party word. Ministers look like politicians but are church ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministers are members of the clergy who lead church services.

clue.text: Place for wild animals always keeping a lot of the other ones upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, which in a down clue turns the letters upside down
keeping means holding within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: A wildlife park where the animals are always upsetting the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild animals' tempts as the wordplay, but the definition is the whole 'Place for wild animals'; 'upset' in a down clue means read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature reserve is protected land where wild animals live safely.

clue.text: For one Guardian leader on top teacher, it's intellectual

parts.note: e.g. means for example

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the newspaper's name
the head teacher runs a school

explanation.surface: A Guardian editorial praising a top teacher as an intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal, slightly mocking word for a bookish intellectual.

clue.text: Married Australian brought in character not from Oz — the fruit of love?

indicators.note: brought in means put inside, so the pair go within the other word

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog from Kansas in The Wizard of Oz
M abbreviates married
A abbreviates Australian

explanation.surface: A married Australian brings home a foreigner, their love producing a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not from Oz' looks like a non-Australian, but Toto appears in Oz without being from there. The 'love apple' was an old name for this fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomatoes were once called love apples, so the tomato is literally the fruit of love.

clue.text: Fine translation of 'sucre' to indicate this?

definitions.text: Fine translation of 'sucre' to indicate this?

indicators.note: a translation renders words in another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neat translation of the French word for sugar would point to this.
explanation.walkthrough: Sucre is French for sugar, so the whole clue also hints at a sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Fructose is the fruit sugar, a kind of sucre in French.

clue.text: Children's programme taking over core of series

indicators.note: taking over means replacing what was there, so one piece displaces another
the core is the middle, which marks the part being swapped out while the ends stay

parts.note: taken as written
prog is a short form of programme

explanation.surface: A children's show takes over as the centrepiece of a TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children's programme' reads as one phrase; split it after Children. Core means the middle letters, which are swapped out. Sprogs is British slang for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprogs is informal British slang for young offspring.

clue.text: Fried potato dish — it's golden when turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A fried potato cake turns golden when flipped in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: Golden brown when turned is just what this dish does in the pan, so the surface hides the reversal well.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a flat cake.

clue.text: It's used for lifting things without tipping?

definitions.text: It's used for lifting things without tipping?

parts.note: surface reading: a hoist or lift for raising goods
setter's reading: a silent server who carries dishes yet never earns a gratuity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' reads as tilting a load, but it means leaving a gratuity: this server is a machine, so no one tips it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lift for carrying food between floors of a restaurant or house, named as a mute serving hand.

clue.text: Tack holding rear of carpet is a bother

indicators.note: holding means gripping within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to tack is to sew with loose stitches

indicators.note: the rear is the back end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Fixing a carpet's back edge with tacks is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack looks like a small nail, but here it is the sewing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is to be in a state of agitation, so a stew is a fuss or bother.

clue.text: Cracker show held in last third of August

indicators.note: held in means contained, so one piece sits inside the other
the last third is the final portion, so only the closing letters are kept

parts.note: the final two of the six letters, a third of the word
an expo is an exhibition or show

explanation.surface: A firework display held in late August.
explanation.walkthrough: A cracker is British slang for a very attractive person, not a firework or biscuit here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexpot is a sexually attractive person, which is what a cracker means in British slang.

clue.text: Stop a party I backed

parts.note: per means a, as in once a day

indicators.note: backed here means moved backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling off a party that I had supported.
explanation.walkthrough: Per can replace a in phrases like ten pounds an hour, so the tiny word a gives three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A period is the American name for a full stop, the punctuation mark.
